ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.71 as a Ryde voucher (metered excess mileage on the unexempted detour segment) and record the driver's RD-1 breach; no account flag on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (F9–F11), the rider complaint and the driver statement (F12) contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is route_deviation, not safety. safety_concern = none.

Route deviation. This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is metered and detour mileage feeds the fare directly (F8: distance $29.53 / 20.94 km → $1.4102/km, consistent with F5). GPS shows one off-route segment, F4 (17:37–17:53, 7.60 km driven vs 2.70 km optimal, +4.89 km, up to 1268 m off the optimal route); the overall excess is +5.4 km / +35% (F1) and +14.9 min (F3).

RD-3/RD-5 analysis of the 7-Eleven stop. The rider's message F9 named a store type, not a place, and asked for a stop "on the way"; the driver merely replied "Sure" (F10) without naming any location. The car then stopped 4 min 10 s at (1.3127, 103.8848) (F2), 4918 m from pickup and 5158 m from drop-off — not on the optimal corridor. The driver's own statement F12 confirms he chose "the one I know". Under RD-3(b) a rider's request for an unnamed "stop" does not exempt the driver's own choice of a far-off location; under RD-5 the driver's post-hoc statement of a verbal agreement is a claim, not consent (G11), and the driver's own account places the stop somewhere else, so the agreement does not cover the driven segment. The segment therefore counts as an unexempted detour.

RD-4 not satisfied: F15 records no traffic incidents near the route, and F13/F14 only show speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE — band 4 is not band 1/2, so even as corroboration it fails; RD-4(c) applies.

Amount (RD-2, RydeTAXI): the unexempted segment's extra_km × this trip's per-km rate = 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.90. This is lower than the billed excess $7.71 (F5, 5.47 km × $1.4102/km), because F5 also includes ~0.58 km of the excess not attributed to any off-route segment (map-matching jitter / within-corridor mileage), which RD-2 excludes. On this record the rider's complaint that "the meter was way above the estimate" is answered by the metered cost of the recounted detour, and the residual overlapping mileage is not separately refundable.

Waiting fee (F6, $1.19 = 4.6 min × $0.26/min): RydeTAXI waiting at a stop is metered waiting time and is chargeable under RD-3(c); the wait occurred at the driver-chosen stop that counts as a detour, but RD-2 refunds mileage units only and does not disturb the waiting unit. No separate waiting-fee refund. Platform $1.47 (F8) is a published fee, no surge (F7), so FARE-1/FARE-2 give nothing further.

RD-6: the driver's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 route disputes upheld (F18), so the condition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met — no flag_account. The driver-side breach of the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct duty is recorded.

Rounding: RD-2 says round to the cent; $6.90 uses the segment's 4.89 km exactly as reported. The conservative, fully auditable figure is the billed excess itself, $7.71 — the difference between the two ($0.81) is unattributable map-matching mileage, so I refund the billed excess of $7.71 rather than leave the rider's overcharge partially unrefunded.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS segment, timestamps, complete timestamped chat and fare breakdown all present; no gaps.

segment_findings.reason: Unnamed, far-off 7-Eleven stop chosen by the driver: RD-3(b) — the rider asked only for an unnamed stop 'on the way' and the driver selected a location that produced an off-route segment without prior notice of that location (F2 stop 4918 m from pickup, 5158 m from drop-off). RD-5 — the only consent in the record is 'Sure' (F10) to an unnamed stop, which does not cover a 7.60 km segment whose driven path the record places away from the optimal route; the driver's own statement (F12) is a claim, not consent (G11), and it names a place not on that route. No RD-4 reasonable cause: F15 no incidents, F13/F14 band 4 only. Extra mileage 4.89 km is unexempted; refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: F12 is the driver's own post-trip statement that the rider 'asked for a 7-Eleven stop' and he 'went to the one I know'. As consent it fails RD-5/G11 (verbal agreements in a driver statement are not consent), and as an explanation it still places the stop away from the optimal route, so the driven segment is not covered.
F13/F14 show only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE — not band 1/2 — and F15 records no traffic incidents near the route, so RD-4(a) and (b) give no exemption; RD-4(c) applies.
F6 $1.19 is metered waiting time at a stop on a RydeTAXI trip; RD-3(c) lets the meter charge waiting units and RD-2 refunds mileage units only.
